name: Roasted Broccoli with Lemon and Garlic Salmon
pitch: You've got salmon and broccoli — roast them together on one pan and dinner basically makes itself.
steps: Preheat your oven to 400°F. While it heats up, cut your broccoli into florets and pat your salmon dry with a paper towel.
Toss the broccoli with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, pepper, and a clove or two of garlic (minced or thinly sliced). Spread it on a sheet pan.
Nestle the salmon fillet(s) right on the same pan. Drizzle a little oil over the salmon and season with salt and pepper.
Roast everything for 15–20 minutes, until the broccoli is tender and a little crispy at the edges and the salmon flakes easily with a fork.
No lemon? A small splash of white vinegar or nothing at all is totally fine — squeeze it over at the end if you have it.

name: Crispy Roasted Broccoli with Chili Flakes
pitch: Simple and satisfying — this broccoli gets genuinely crispy edges in the oven, and pairs perfectly as a side to your salmon.
steps: Preheat your oven to 400°F. Cut the broccoli into bite-sized pieces — don't go too small or they'll burn before they crisp up. The stalks are worth using too; just peel them if they feel tough.
Spread the broccoli on a sheet pan. Add a clove or two of thinly sliced garlic, a light drizzle of oil, and a pinch of salt. Toss it all with your hands right on the pan.
No red pepper flakes? A pinch of regular chili powder or just black pepper works fine — or skip it entirely.
Roast for about 10–12 minutes, shaking the pan once or twice. Watch the garlic — you want it golden, not dark brown. Pull it when the edges of the broccoli look a little charred and delicious.
Serve alongside your salmon for a fuss-free weeknight plate.

name: Garlic Butter Salmon with Roasted Broccoli
pitch: Salmon and broccoli are honestly a dream team — a little garlic butter ties them together into a simple, satisfying dinner that feels way fancier than the effort it takes.
steps: Preheat your oven to 425°F (220°C). Cut the broccoli into florets, toss with oil, salt, and pepper, and spread on a baking sheet. Pop it in the oven for about 20 minutes, flipping once halfway through.
While the broccoli roasts, pat your salmon dry and season both sides with salt and pepper. Heat a splash of oil in a skillet over medium-high heat.

Cook the salmon skin-side up for about 3–4 minutes until golden, then flip. Add a knob of butter and a couple of minced garlic cloves to the pan and spoon the garlicky butter over the salmon as it finishes cooking, another 3–4 minutes depending on thickness.
Plate the salmon alongside the roasted broccoli and drizzle any pan butter over the top. Simple but genuinely delicious.
toolSuggestion: A cast iron or stainless steel skillet for a great sear on the salmon
